name: ccz_shared_pair_phase_polynomial_fusion
precondition: family dv_recon; Toffoli-level op list over x / cx / cz / z / t / tdg / ccx / ccz / h only (no rz, no measurement, no gadget), containing at least two ccz (or ccx, read as h-ccz-h on its target) and at least one cx, 6 <= qubits <= 34. Needs toffoli. Runs unitarily, no ancilla_room needed. A circuit with no ccz, or with fewer than two ccz inside any common Hadamard-free region, is excluded and costs nothing.
identity: Degree-3 phase-polynomial column merge. In a Hadamard-free region every ccz/cz/z/t is diagonal and therefore commutes with every other diagonal gate; only cx and x act linearly on the wires. So the region's action is: a GF(2)-affine map on the wires, times the diagonal phase exp(i*pi*f(x)) where f is a polynomial over GF(2)-affine parity labels, and `phasepoly.labels` gives each wire's label (mask, const) at every position. Read each ccz at position p on wires (u,v,w) as the cubic monomial P*Q*R where P,Q,R are the affine labels of u,v,w at p. The identity used is, for any three parities, (-1)^{PQR} * (-1)^{PQS} = (-1)^{PQ(R xor S)}, because the two exponents differ only when R=S=1, where their sum is even. Hence two ccz gates whose label triples agree on two slots, {P,Q,R} and {P,Q,S}, fuse into ONE ccz on (P, Q, R xor S): emit cx(c -> d) ; ccz(a, b, d) ; cx(c -> d) on representative wires a,b,c,d carrying P,Q,R,S (and, if R xor S is already the label of some live wire, even the two cx's are unnecessary). Two ccz become one ccz plus at most two cx: 14 T -> 7 T. The procedure does this globally rather than pairwise: for each maximal Hadamard-free region, collect the multiset of cubic monomials, cancel duplicates outright (P*Q*R twice = identity, 14 T -> 0 T), then greedily build a maximum matching on the graph whose vertices are the remaining monomials and whose edges join monomials sharing two labels, fusing each matched pair; repeat to fixpoint, since a fused monomial can share a pair with a third. Finally re-emit the region as (linear cx/x skeleton) + (one ccz per surviving cubic monomial, parities materialised by cx conjugation) + the region's original affine map restored.
correctness: Three independent exact arguments, all available inside the frozen API. (1) Algebraic: inside a Hadamard-free region the circuit is exactly (affine permutation) x (diagonal phase in the parity labels); the fusion identity above is an equality of GF(2) exponents, checked term by term, so the diagonal factor is unchanged as a function on all basis states, and the affine factor is restored because each conjugating cx is emitted in an undone pair. Global phase is untouched (all gates are real diagonal signs). (2) Proof-carrying: `phasepoly.witness(old_region_ops, new_region_ops, n)` is exactly a proof of equivalence for the Hadamard-free class in O(ops) with no matrices - the rewrite is only kept when the witness returns ok, so no application rests on my algebra. (3) Judge: both sides are Clifford+T (ccz lowers to 7 T), so the frozen verifier checks the changed window exactly over D[omega], and the whole-circuit pass re-checks against the ORIGINAL circuit. Hadamards are never crossed: regions come from `segments(ops, cut=('h',))` intersected with the wires each ccz touches, so no commutation through h is ever assumed. ccx is handled as h(target) ccz h(target), which is an exact rewrite, and the flanking h's are reabsorbed when the ccz re-emerges on the same target wire.
trigger: Fires once per maximal Hadamard-free region, at most once per region per pass. For each region: (1) run `phasepoly.labels` / `rotation_labels` over its ops to get the affine label of every wire at every position and the cubic monomial (as a sorted triple of label keys) of every ccz in it; (2) count monomials - emit a match if either (a) some monomial occurs an even number of times (free cancellation), or (b) at least one pair of distinct monomials shares two of its three labels; (3) the match carries the region bounds plus the chosen cancellation set and matching, computed deterministically (monomials ordered by label key, greedy matching in that order) so apply() is pure. Decline if the region has fewer than two ccz, or if no pair shares two labels, or if the re-emitted region does not price strictly lower, or if `witness` declines.
expected_effect: This circuit is a carry-lookahead adder: its 57 ccz are generate/propagate products p_i*g_j recomputed across a tree, and the fingerprint already reports 44 shared_control_pairs - i.e. 44 ccz pairs that agree on two of three arguments, which is exactly this rule's edge set. Each fused pair deletes one ccz = 7 T and adds at most 2 cx (cx is not priced before T in the lexicographic order). A greedy matching on 44 overlapping edges over 57 vertices realistically fuses ~20 pairs, and the uncompute half of the lookahead tree supplies outright duplicate monomials that cancel to 0 T. Estimate: 57 ccz -> ~37 ccz, 399 T -> ~259 T, with the h-count unchanged and the cx-count rising by at most ~40. The surviving ccz are the ones whose argument triples are pairwise disjoint, which is the genuine degree-3 content of the adder's phase polynomial - pyzx's full_reduce works on the ZX graph and does not perform this cubic-column merge, so the saving is not a repeat of the floor's pyzx-class rotation merging (which is degree-1 Pauli-axis merging and has zero headroom here), and it is unitary and exact, so it does not touch the ancilla_reconstruction lever that was already consumed.
source: Heyfron and Campbell, 'An efficient quantum compiler that reduces T count', Quantum Sci. Technol. 4, 015004 (2019) - TODD, Third Order Duplicate and Destroy, merging columns of the degree-3 signature tensor of a CNOT+T circuit; Amy, Maslov and Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning', IEEE TCAD 33(10) (2014) - the phase-polynomial representation of Hadamard-free regions; Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), appendix - the CCZ(a,b,c)CCZ(a,b,d) = cx(c,d) CCZ(a,b,d) cx(c,d) shared-control identity.
